Aspacanah-, Vistaspa-; Av. aspa-, Skt. бра, 
Lt. equos. 

pIE *yikuo-, OP visa- ‘all’, also in visadahyu-; 
OP nspa- (with Med. sp) in vispaeana-; Av. 
vispa-, Skt. visva-. 

vi- prefix ‘away, apart’: Av. vi, Skt. vi; with 
verbal roots kan-, jan-, iar-, nof-, mard-, and 
perhaps in sbb. Vidarna-, Vivdna-, Vistaspa-, and 
adj. Viyaxna-. 


við- sb. ‘house, royal house, royal clan, court’ 
(JNES 4232): Av. vis- ‘Herrenhaus’, Skt. vié- 
‘house, dwelling’, Gk. ofxos ‘house’, Lt. vicus 
‘village’ (§22, $87, $114, §142). Decl., §188.1V, 
visa- adj. ‘all’: OP (Med.) vispa-, Av. vispa-, 
Skt. víóva-, pAr. *yiSya- (800) for pIE *uiko- 
(OCS vist ‘all’) after -ya- in (Skt.) sdrva- (see OP 
haruva-; 5150). See also visadahyu-, and cf. viba-, 
vispa-.  visahyü gsm. DSa 5; DS} 6. visam nsn. 
DSj 4°; DSI 5. visam asn. DNa 49; DSf 21; DSi 
4°; XPa 16; XPb 25f; XPf 42; XPh 44. 


visadahyu- adj. ‘of or for all countries or 
provinces’ ($161.Па): borrowed in Elam. mz-25- 
ía-da-a-hu-i$ and (with Med. vispa-) Akk. u~- 
1$-pt-da-a-'-1; visa- ‘all’ + dahyu- ‘country, prov- 
ince’. visadahyum asm. (§53, 418811) XPa 12. 


vispa- adj. ‘all’: Median (49.11, $90) for OP 
visa-, q.v. See also wtspazana-. vispā absn. 
A%Sa 5°; Ada 4, Аас 4 (iispa db, $55.1); 
A?Ha 6°. 


vispazana- adj. ‘containing all (kinds of) men’ 
($101.09): borrowed in Elam. mi-iš-ša-da-na, 
from the OP form *visadana-: Med. vispa- ‘all’ + 
Med. zana- ‘man, human being’ ($9.11, §88, $90). 
uspazananim gpf. DNa 10Ї; DSe 9f; DZc 5.

- 1769, "broad street or promenade planted with rows of trees," from French boulevard , originally "top surface of a military rampart" (15c.), from a garbled attempt to adopt Middle Dutch bolwerc "wall of a fortification" (see bulwark ) into French, which at that time lacked a -w- in its alphabet.

- The notion is of a promenade atop demolished city walls, which would be wider than the old streets. Originally in English with conscious echoes of Paris; in U.S., since 1929, used of multi-lane limited-access urban highways. Early French attempts to digest the Dutch word also include boloart , boulever , boloirque , and bollvercq .

- early 15c., "a fortification outside a city wall or gate; a rampart, barricade," from Middle Dutch bulwerke or Middle High German bolwerc , probably [Skeat] from bole "plank, tree trunk" (from Proto-Germanic *bul- , from PIE root *bhel- (2) "to blow, swell") + werc "work" (see work (n.)). Thus "bole-work," a construction of logs. Figurative sense "means of defense or security" is from mid-15c. A doublet of boulevard .
- 1856, a French word in English, "one who frequents the boulevard ;" i.e. "man-about-town, one fond of urban living and society."

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

content.content:
# Proto-Indo-European *wí

**Etymology:**
The term is "likely from *dwi-, with *d dropped, or possibly shifted to a *h₁ sound due to the Kortlandt effect."

**Meaning:**
The adverb conveys two senses: (1) "apart" or "asunder," and (2) "away from" or "against."

**Key Derivatives:**

- **Indo-Iranian *wí**: Descended directly, appearing in Sanskrit as विना (vínā, "without, except")

- ***wi-tero-* compounds**: Forms meaning "further apart," yielding Latin vitricus and generating widespread descendants

- **Germanic *wiþrą**: Derived from the adverbial accusative form *wíterom, meaning "toward, against; compared to, among"

- **Avestan vītarəm**: An Indo-Iranian adverbial form meaning "again, further"

- **Proto-Slavic *vъtorъ**: Meaning "second," traced through Balto-Slavic intermediates

- **Latin derivatives**: vitium ("fault, vice") and vitupero ("vituperate") reflect the sense of aberration or deviation

These forms demonstrate the prefix's widespread use across Indo-European languages to express separation, distinction, and directionality.

# Etymology Section

[Inherited](/wiki/Appendix:Glossary#inherited "Appendix:Glossary") from [Middle Persian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Persian "w:Middle Persian") \[script needed\] (wtʾhtn' /⁠widāxtan⁠/), from [Proto-Iranian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proto-Iranian_language "w:Proto-Iranian language") _[\*wi-](/w/index.php?title=Reconstruction:Proto-Iranian/wi-&action=edit&redlink=1 "Reconstruction:Proto-Iranian/wi- (page does not exist)")_ + _[\*taHč-](/w/index.php?title=Reconstruction:Proto-Iranian/taH%C4%8Dati&action=edit&redlink=1 "Reconstruction:Proto-Iranian/taHčati (page does not exist)")_ ("to melt"), from [Proto-Indo-European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proto-Indo-European_language "w:Proto-Indo-European language") _[\*teh₂-k-](/wiki/Reconstruction:Proto-Indo-European/teh%E2%82%82- "Reconstruction:Proto-Indo-European/teh₂-")_ ("to melt"), cognate with [Northern Kurdish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurmanji "w:Kurmanji") _[bihatin](/w/index.php?title=bihatin&action=edit&redlink=1 "bihatin (page does not exist)")_, _[bihoştin](/w/index.php?title=biho%C5%9Ftin&action=edit&redlink=1 "bihoştin (page does not exist)")_ ("to melt"). Compare [Ancient Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek "w:Ancient Greek") _[τήκω](/wiki/%CF%84%CE%AE%CE%BA%CF%89#Ancient_Greek "τήκω")_ (tḗkō, "to melt").

# English Etymology of "Wide"

From Middle English *wid*, *wyd*, from Old English *wīd* ("wide, vast, broad, long; distant, far"), from Proto-Germanic *\*wīdaz*, from Proto-Indo-European *\*h₁weydʰh₁-* ("to divide, separate").

The PIE root represents "a dissimilated univerbation from *\*dwi-* ('apart, asunder, in two') +‎ *\*dʰeh₁-* ('to do, put, place')."

lines: + From Proto-Indo-European *gʰrebh₂- ( “ to grab, seize ” ) . Cognates include Persian گرفتن ( gereftan ) , Central Kurdish گرتن ( girtin ) , Sanskrit गृह्णाति ( gṛhṇāti , “ he seizes ” ) .
+ Persian Wikipedia has an article on: گرگ

+ Inherited from Middle Persian 𐭢𐭥𐭫𐭢 ( gʿlg /⁠gurg⁠/ , “ wolf ” ) , from Old Persian 𐎺𐎼𐎣 ( v-r-k /⁠varka-⁠/ ) , from Proto-Iranian *wŕ̥kah , from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wŕ̥kas , from Proto-Indo-European *wĺ̥kʷos , possibly from *wl̥kʷós ( “ dangerous ” , adjective ) .
+ گرگ • ( gurg / gorg ) ( plural گرگ‌ها ( gurg-hā / gorg-hâ ) , or گرگان ( gurgān / gorgân ) , Tajik spelling гург )

+ c. 1260s , Jalāl ad-Dīn Mohammad Rūmī , translated by Reynold A. Nicholson , مثنوی معنوی [ Masnavi-ye-Ma'navi ], volume I, verse 3109: از کجا آموختی این ای بزرگ / گفت ای شاه جهان از حال گرگ‌‌ az kujâ âmôxti ên ay buzurg / guft ay šâh-i-jahân az hâl-i- gurg Whence didst thou learn this, O eminent one?” “O King of the world,” he replied, “from the fate of the wolf .”
+ ( figurative ) a social or sexual predator
+ اون بیرون پر گرگه! ― un birun por-e gorg -e! ― There are lots of predator s out there!
+ گرگ‌ِ بالان‌دیده ( gorg-e bâlân-dide , “ a highly seasoned person ” )
+ گرگ‌ِ بیابان ( gorg-e biâbân , “ steppe wolf ” )
+ گرگ‌ِ تاسمانی ( gorg-e tâsmâni , “ Tasmanian wolf ” )
+ Hayyim, Sulayman ( 1934 ), “ گرڭ ”, in New Persian–English dictionary , Teheran: Librairie-imprimerie Béroukhim
+ Dehkhoda, Ali-Akbar ( 1931– ), “ گرگ ”, in Dehkhoda Dictionary Institute , editors, Dehkhoda Dictionary (in Persian), Tehran: University of Tehran Press .

Page 554 (book page 524, root Wi, part 2) is verified. `verify_check.py 554` reports 13 of 13 nodes done and no PROBLEM lines.

- **Root Wi:** confirmed (Pokorny 1175-1176; Walde-Pokorny I 312f.; Watkins/AHD).
- **Node verdicts:** 5 confirmed, 7 plausible, 1 transcription_suspect, 0 disputed.

**transcription_suspect (the book's error, not the extraction's)**
- Node #6 (Avestan) "ôithara: lonely": there is no such Avestan word. Gharib's entry for Sogdian 'yw-wšy "lonely" cites Av. viθra, so the book prints "ôithara" where it should have viθra.

**Other issues worth knowing (all marked plausible)**
- Node #2: the "vi-taxtî ☞Dhogh" cross-reference goes against Cheung (*taHč "melt") and Nyberg (vi + tak- "run"). "vi-vačah" and "vi-kar" are reconstructions, not attested Avestan words.
- Node #3 (govârdan): Aryanpur derives it from *gʷer- "swallow", not from vi- + kar-.
- Node #3's own references point to the wrong pages. BQT:1813 and 1835 hold Part 1's words (گزیدن، گمیختن). This node's words are on BQT ≈1717 (گواژه), 1777 (گداختن) and ≈1851 (گواردن).
- Node #5 (vîspa "all"): only Pokorny links it to *wi-; Kent and Wiktionary do not. Also, "vîspa-dahyu" is the Old Persian/Median visadahyu-, not an Avestan word.
- Nodes #11 and #12 (wide from *wi-itos): this is the AHD/Klein/Buck view. Wiktionary prefers *h₁weydʰh₁-.
